sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Bonded Warehouse Operations in Customs Free Trade Zones

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Roman-Germanic tradition with French Napoleonic codification influence; unitary national law; no sub-state tax distinction)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: BLEU (Belgium-Luxembourg Economic Union) - China Bilateral Investment Treaty (in force 5 February 1986)
Luxembourg - China Double Taxation Agreement (DTA signed 14 March 1994, in force 28 June 1995, as modified by the OECD Multilateral Instrument effective 1 January 2020)
EU-China Comprehensive Agreement on Investment (signed 30 December 2020; provisional application suspended pending ratification)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing (as amended, transposing EU Directives 2015/849 and 2018/843); Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE); CSSF Regulation No. 12-02 of 14 December 2012 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing (as amended); Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies (Articles 711-1 to 711-9 on UBO identification and share registers).
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_note: Access to the Luxembourg RBE is restricted to competent authorities and obliged entities demonstrating a legitimate interest, following the CJEU judgments of 22 November 2022 (C-37/20 WM and C-601/20 Sovim). Beneficial ownership particulars are not publicly searchable.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of valid passport or national identity document of each shareholder, director (gérant) and beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent passport or identity authority of the country of origin; the copy must be certified by a notary or government registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (for states party to the 1961 Hague Convention) OR Consular Legalization at the Luxembourg Embassy or Consulate (for non-Hague jurisdictions)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement issued within the last 3 months) for each shareholder and manager
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or licensed bank in the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization (as applicable)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good conduct (extrait du casier judiciaire / police clearance certificate) for each manager (gérant) and natural-person shareholder with control
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Criminal records authority or Ministry of Justice of the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Corporate resolution of the corporate shareholder authorizing the SARL incorporation, capital subscription, and appointment of managers (authenticated extract of minutes)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate shareholder's board or notary, and, if applicable, home-country trade registry

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation and current extract of the register (or equivalent) proving legal existence of any corporate shareholder
Bank reference letter confirming good standing and source of funds for the initial capital contribution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Deposit-taking bank in the shareholder's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized signature of the bank officer; Apostille or Consular Legalization only where expressly demanded by the Luxembourg notary or the CSSF

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory automated screening of all shareholders, managers, UBOs and authorized signatories against the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UN Security Council Sanctions Lists, OFAC SDN List, and the Luxembourg FIU reference files; PEP identification under Article 2(d) of the Law of 12 November 2004; enhanced due diligence mandatory for PEPs, high-risk third countries identified by FATF, and transactions involving cash-intensive or cross-border trade corridors.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS); portal https://www.lbr.lu; electronic filing via the RCS e-file module and publication in the RESA (Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must be written in Roman or Latin characters; French is the operative language of the RCS, but a name in any EU or global language is accepted if transliterated into Latin script. For a SARL, the corporate name must be immediately preceded or followed by 'Société à responsabilité limitée' or the abbreviation 'SARL'. A name identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name is refused under the Law of 10 August 1915 and the doctrine of unicity of corporate denomination.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque / Bank / Crédit / Caisse (requires prior CSSF license and ministerial authorization)
Assurance / Assureur / Réassurance (requires prior Commissariat aux Assurances authorization)
Fonds / Investment Fund / SICAV (requires CSSF authorization under the 2010 UCI law)
Bourse / Stock Exchange / Clearing House (requires special government concession)
État / Grand-Duché / Ministère / Commune / Luxembourg (misleading state affiliation)
Société Anonyme / S.A. / S.A.R.L. used by another corporate form (misleading legal-form indication)
Free Zone / Entrepôt (sensitive token; acceptable only upon production of the customs authorization for the bonded depot)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Luxembourg law does not provide a de jure statutory name-reservation system. The RCS performs the formal non-confusion check at the time of the initial filing of the notarial deed. If the name is rejected: (i) the notary amends or re-executes the articles of association substituting the name, and (ii) a new RCS filing is submitted. Against an explicit refusal, an administrative appeal lies with the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg (commercial chamber) within 2 months of the notification; an urgent interim injunction (référé) is available where imminent prejudice is demonstrated. Practitioners should obtain an updated LBR negative search certificate before any re-filing.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Partially permissible for a pure holding or administrative SARL through an approved domiciliation agent (fiduciaire) under the law of 19 December 2008 and CSSF circular practice. Not permissible for this bonded-depot business scope: the Administration des douanes et accises (Luxembourg Customs) requires a physical, staffed bonded warehouse inside a customs free zone or entrepôt, with direct customs-access guarantees and records. A virtual office cannot satisfy the customs commercial-substance test.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High (estimated 70% probability of an unannounced customs physical inspection within the first 12 months of operations); additional on-site checks by the RCS or CSSF on registered-office substance and by the Ministry of the Economy under the trade-licensing regime (estimated 20% probability in year one).

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Public name search and RCS pre-incorporation negative name check via LBR online portal
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fee: free online search; optional certified extract approximately EUR 5 (market benchmark)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial deed of incorporation (statuts) including mandatory anti-money-laundering verification of shareholders and UBOs
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary of the Chambre des Notaires du Luxembourg
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Regulated notarial tariff (Law of 9 December 1976); market benchmark EUR 1,500 - 2,500 per standard SARL deed

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille or consular legalization of six foreign-origin documents (passports, address proofs, sanctions, resolutions, registry extracts)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent authority of the country of origin (e.g., Secretary of State or foreign ministry) or Luxembourg consular post
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Hague Convention fee schedule; consular fees vary by post; market benchmark USD 25 per authentication

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS registration fee and mandatory publication in the RESA electronic journal
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fixed duty of EUR 80 for incorporation filing and publication (fee schedule of LBR)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Register of Beneficial Owners
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fee: free of charge under the Law of 13 January 2019

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Trade licence (autorisation d'établissement) application fee for warehouse and storage activity
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of the Economy - General Directorate for SMEs and Classes Moyennes
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fee of EUR 85 under the Law of 2 September 2011 on the access to professions

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Customs bonded warehouse authorization advisory (UCC Articles 240-241; AEO and comprehensive guarantee assessment)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed customs agent or customs consultancy (market) in coordination with the Administration des douanes et accises
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark; no statutory state fee for the authorization application; customs guarantee underwriting costs separate

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/KYC PEP and sanctions screening database subscription (annual)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Commercial AML screening provider (LSEG/World-Check, Dow Jones, or equivalent)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark EUR 300 - 800 per entity per year; one-year subscription for pre-incorporation and ongoing screening

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certificate of good conduct (casier judiciaire) for each manager, including apostille
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Judicial authority of the country of origin
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Government fee; typically USD 20 - 50 per certificate plus apostille fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office / domiciliation agreement (first quarter reserve)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark EUR 150 - 250 per month; first-quarter deposit

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: External counsel review of statuts, UBO structure, and bonded-warehouse licensing memorandum
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark fixed fee EUR 1,200 - 2,000 for combined company-law and AML/CFT regulatory scope

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended, Articles 180 to 190-1 (SARL regime); Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies and on the Book-keeping and Annual Accounts of Undertakings; Law of 23 September 2011 on the electronic RCS; UCC Regulation (EU) 952/2013 Articles 211 and 243 (customs warehousing and free zones).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), under the authority of the Ministry of Justice.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial deed of incorporation (acte constitutif) executed before a Luxembourg notary, electronically filed with the RCS and published in the electronic official gazette RESA (Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital EUR 12,000 (Article 182-1, Law of 10 August 1915), fully subscribed at incorporation; each in-cash quota must be paid up to at least 25% immediately, non-cash contributions fully paid upon execution; the entire subscribed cash capital must be deposited in a blocked escrow account (compte bloqué) at a Luxembourg or EEA credit institution and released only after RCS registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the initial shareholders, having duly subscribed the entire share capital of EUR 12,000, hereby adopt the Articles of Incorporation executed before the Luxembourg notary this day; that the company's registered office is fixed at [address], Luxembourg, Grand Duchy of Luxembourg; that Mr./Ms. [Name] is hereby appointed as sole Manager (Gérant) of the company with full powers to act within the corporate purpose; that the blocked capital deposit certificate issued by [Bank] is approved and released to the company upon RCS registration; that the Manager is authorized to execute all filings with the RCS, RESA, customs and tax authorities, and to sign the bond required for the customs warehousing authorization.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve corporate name and open blocked capital account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) name-availability portal; Luxembourg or EEA credit institution.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Verify availability of the proposed corporate name via the RCS electronic search and reserve it if necessary. Open a blocked escrow account in the name of the company to be formed (société en formation) at a Luxembourg or EEA bank and deposit the minimum subscribed capital of EUR 12,000. Obtain the bank blocked-funds attestation (certificat de blocage) naming the notary as beneficiary and evidencing the deposit and blocking conditions.
required_dossiers: Optional RCS name-reservation confirmation
Certified passports of all incorporators
Preliminary draft articles of association
Bank KYC forms and source-of-funds declarations
Blocked-funds certificate issued by the credit institution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries the source of funds, submit certified bank statements and a notarial AML declaration; any such requiry extends the timeline by up to 5 business days; if the certificate expires, the bank re-issues a renewed blocked-funds attestation prior to notarial execution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute the notarial deed of incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary appointed within the arrondissement of Luxembourg or Diekirch (Chambre des Notaires du Luxembourg).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary reviews the draft articles (statuts), verifies compliance with the Law of 10 August 1915 as amended, confirms payment of the share capital against the blocked-funds certificate, and performs mandatory KYC/AML screening of shareholders and the future manager. The deed is read aloud and signed by all shareholders and the appointed manager, creating a legal entity upon RCS registration.
required_dossiers: Final draft articles of association (statuts)
Blocked-funds certificate
Certified passports of shareholders and manager
Criminal record extract (extrait du casier judiciaire) of the manager
Beneficial-ownership statement for the future register of beneficial owners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: The notary requests any missing or corrected supporting documents from the parties; if the capital deposit certificate has lapsed, a refreshed blocked-funds attestation must be obtained before signature; the notarial schedule is then reset by the number of days required to cure the deficiency.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronically file with the RCS and publish in RESA
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS e-filing portal, rcs.lu) under the Ministry of Justice.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 15 days of signature, the notary transmits the deed and the standard filing forms to the RCS electronically, paying the statutory fee of EUR 19. The RCS registrar validates the file, issues the RCS registration number and the national identification number (NIF), and causes the extract to be published in the electronic gazette RESA. Legal personality becomes effective on registration.
required_dossiers: Signed notarial deed (digital reproducible copy)
RCS standard registration form
Corporate object statement reflecting ISIC 5210 bonded warehouse and free-zone activity
Proof of payment of the RCS filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a request for completion (demande de complément), the notary amends and re-files within the prescribed deadline; a refusal may be challenged before the District Court of Luxembourg (Tribunal d'arrondissement) by summary proceedings, or the deed is rectified by a subsequent notarial act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register for tax, VAT and social security
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD); Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AED); Centre commun de la sécurité sociale (CCSS).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS registration, file the corporate tax registration return with the ACD to open the income tax and municipal business tax file; register with the AED for Luxembourg VAT purposes (standard rate 17%); register as employer with the CCSS to obtain the employer social security number, and file the joint VAT and employer declarations through the guichet unique (MyGuichet.lu).
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract
Notarial deed of incorporation
Registered office acceptance and lease confirmation
Manager and beneficial-owner identification forms
Bank account confirmation for treasury operations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the ACD or AED raises an objection to the registration data, the company files a rectified declaration or a spontaneous regularization; administrative fines for late registration are avoidable by filing the corrected return within the grace period and submitting a reasoned explanation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain commercial establishment authorization and customs bonded-depot permit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministère de l'Économie - Direction générale des classes moyennes; Administration des douanes et accises (Customs and Excise Administration).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the business establishment authorization (autorisation d'établissement) for the warehouse and logistics activity where applicable; simultaneously file an application with the Customs and Excise Administration for a customs warehousing authorization under Article 211 UCC and, where the bonded depot is located in a free zone, for free-zone status under Article 243 UCC. Submit the premises layout, stock control procedures, access-security plan, and a financial guarantee or surety bond covering potential customs debt.
required_dossiers: Business establishment application form
Certificate of good conduct and professional competence of the applicant
Title or lease of the bonded depot premises
Site plan with bonded area demarcation
UCC Article 211 customs warehouse authorization application
Financial guarantee instrument or customs surety bond
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where the customs administration requests additional information, submit the clarification within 30 days and, if refused, lodge an appeal with the Director of the Customs and Excise Administration within 3 months and thereafter with the Administrative Tribunal of Luxembourg.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Économie - Direction générale des classes moyennes (business establishment authorization); Administration des douanes et accises (customs warehouse and free-zone operating authorization).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement (business establishment permit) combined with the UCC Article 211 customs warehousing authorization and Article 243 free-zone status (entrepôt douanier / zone franche) constituting the bonded-depot operating license.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement - Ministry of the Environment, Climate and Biodiversity
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 4 Commodo/Incommodo declaration administered at commune level under the Law of 9 May 2014 on the prevention and management of environmental nuisances; a full EIA report is mandatory only where the bonded depot stores dangerous substances exceeding the Seveso III thresholds (Law of 10 June 1999 on major-accident prevention).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Trade-effluent discharges limited to BOD5 ≤ 25 mg/L, COD ≤ 125 mg/L, TSS ≤ 30 mg/L, pH 6.5-8.5 and mineral oils ≤ 5 mg/L under grand-ducal water-discharge regulations; VOC emissions controlled to BAT-AELs under Directive 2010/75/EU where solvent and storage thresholds are met; all waste movements documented in a statutory waste register and bordereaux de suivi des déchets (BSD) under the Law of 21 March 2012 on waste management.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety certification and site clearance issued by the communal fire brigade / Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours (CGDIS); workplace health-and-safety inspection and occupational clearance by the Inspection du travail et des mines (ITM) under the Luxembourg Labour Code, including structural load inspection of racking systems by an approved engineering bureau; additional civil-defense site approval required where hazardous goods are stored within the bonded area.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct taxation; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for registration duties and VAT; primary electronic portal is MyGuichet.lu, with company registration through the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign owners establishing an SARL must (i) execute a notarial deed of incorporation, (ii) file for incorporation with the RCS via the Luxembourg Business Registers e-desk, (iii) obtain the RCS registration number, which serves as the national identification number / matricule and functional TIN, and (iv) apply separately for a Luxembourg VAT identification number by submitting the standard VAT registration form through MyGuichet.lu, executed by the appointed local manager or authorised tax representative. The VAT number is notified in writing after verification of the registered office, beneficial ownership declarations, and supporting KYC documents from non-resident shareholders.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not operate a check-the-box classification system; an SARL is per se taxable at entity level. Elective mechanisms include fiscal unity (intégration fiscale) for direct taxes under Article 164bis of the Income Tax Law (LIR), VAT grouping (assujetti unique) under Article 59 of the Luxembourg VAT Law, and limited elections under tax incentive regimes. Hybrid mismatch rules are neutralised through the ATAD implementation; there is no elective hybrid mismatch instrument.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general minimum turnover threshold for mandatory VAT registration of taxable supplies made in Luxembourg; however, the small business exemption applies to Luxembourg-established businesses with annual turnover not exceeding EUR 30,000 (exclusive of VAT). For non-established suppliers, intra-Community distance sales of goods exceeding EUR 35,000 trigger Luxembourg VAT registration, subject to the electronic OSS regime election.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg does not require real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or government API validation for B2B invoices. E-invoicing is mandatory only for business-to-government (B2G) supplies, using the PEPPOL interoperability framework. For all other supplies, taxpayers must ensure the authenticity and integrity of invoices through business controls. VAT returns and recapitulative statements are filed electronically through the AEDT portal; there is no national clearance stamping regime.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to: (i) direct export supplies of goods transported or dispatched outside the EU where the supplier retains documentary evidence of physical departure; (ii) supplies of goods under customs bonded-warehouse arrangements or free-zone procedures where the goods remain under customs suspension and are destined for extra-EU export; (iii) intra-Community supplies of goods where the customer communicates a valid EU/ Luxembourg VAT identification number and the goods are dispatched to another Member State; and (iv) services that are directly linked to exported goods or supplied to non-EU customers in accordance with place-of-supply rules. The taxpayer must obtain and preserve all substantive evidence of the physical flow, export customs clearance, transport, and payment matching before applying the 0% rate.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Single Administrative Document (SAD/DAU) export customs declaration with authenticated MRN
Bill of Lading, air waybill, or CMR road consignment note evidencing physical cross-border carriage
Proof of arrival or acceptance by the non-EU customs authority or frontier documentation
Commercial invoice and packing list identifying the goods, quantities, and ultimate destination
VAT ID and VIES/ECS records for intra-Community supplies where relevant
Inward remittance certificate or bank settlement evidence matching invoice amounts and customs declarations
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT and the Luxembourg Customs and Excise Administration conduct cross-matched audits of export declarations, MRN records, transport documentation, and bank inflows. Where zero-rating is claimed with missing, inconsistent, or fraudulent documentation, the export treatment is reversed, 17% VAT becomes chargeable, late interest accrues from the date of supply, and the VAT refund is clawed back. Administrative penalties and criminal sanctions may be imposed for tax fraud, including fines and imprisonment of up to 10 years for deliberate abuse. The standard reassessment period is 5 years, extended to 10 years in cases of fraudulent intent.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) — Luxembourg's national central bank and a member of the Eurosystem. BCL exercises monetary-policy functions, TARGET2 membership, and oversight of payment, clearing, and settlement systems. Prudential supervision of credit institutions and electronic money institutions is delegated to the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Euro (EUR) is fully convertible on both current and capital accounts under EU law (TFEU Article 63). Luxembourg imposes no foreign-exchange control approval, no classified capital vs. current-account permit regime, and no prior central-bank consent for wire transfers. Profit remittance, dividend distribution, loan repayments, and liquidation proceeds to non-resident shareholders are unrestricted. The only administrative obligation is the statistical balance-of-payments (BOP) reporting to BCL for cross-border payments above certain de minimis thresholds.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Luxembourg imposes no export-proceeds surrender, repatriation, or mandatory conversion rules. Bonded warehouse and free-zone sales receipts may be retained in any freely convertible currency without time limits or conversion ratios. Periodic BOP statistical declaration to the BCL is the only compliance requirement; no statutory timeline or ratio applies to EUR conversion.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (Spuerkeess / BCEE)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility for EU-passported electronic money institutions (EMIs) such as PayPal, Mangopay, or Banking Circle: they can handle low-value settlements and payroll, but generally cannot hold segregated customs-duties funds, issue documentary trade instruments, or act as principal treasury counterparty for bonded-depot operations. Low feasibility for offshore, non-EU EMIs without CSSF passporting: such providers are not authorised to hold client monies or open settlement accounts in Luxembourg and will be rejected at the KYC/UBO stage.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No Luxembourg statute mandates physical attendance of directors for account opening, but bank policy universally requires an in-person or remote identification interview for medium-risk sectors such as free-zone bonded depots. In practice, the managing director or a Luxembourg-authorised agent with signature power must appear before the bank's acceptance committee in a physical meeting; non-EU UBOs may be covered by dual video-identification plus apostilled documentation, yet most major banks insist on one in-person meeting before onboarding is completed.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque, multi-layered ownership structure with non-EU trusts, foundations, or holding companies above the SARL.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: RCS Luxembourg excerpt; Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE) extract showing ultimate beneficial owners; complete organisational chart with percentage holdings; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds declarations per UBO; audited parent-company financial statements; notarised corporate resolutions evidencing ownership history.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Free-trade-zone and bonded-warehouse industry classification flagged as enhanced risk for customs-duty evasion, shadow inventory, and invoice-fraud schemes.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Customs approved warehousing authorisation under the Union Customs Code; Valid EORI certificate; lease or concession contract on the bonded depot within the free zone; stock-management software audit trail; periodic inventory reconciliation reports signed by a Luxembourg certified auditor; T1 transit declarations and customs entry/exit documentation; VAT identification certificate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large and frequent cross-border capital injections, inbound shareholder loans, or high-value wire turnover inconsistent with the declared storage-only business profile.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised capital-increase minutes and share-transfer deeds; statutory minimum capital of €12,000 fully evidenced as paid-up; banking records confirming the source of physical funds; pro-forma invoices, warehouse receipts, and Bills of Lading proving the trade flow; ISDA/FBF derivative master agreements if hedging transactions are expected; advance tax ruling or tax-residency certificate from the Luxembourg Ministry of Finance if applicable.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity subscriptions and shareholder-loan disbursements are routed by SWIFT MT103 to the SARL's EUR-denominated account at a Luxembourg credit institution. The wire must carry the ECB/BOP purpose code 'S110' for direct-investment equity capital or 'S120' for shareholder loans to enable BCL statistical classification. No CSSF or BCL foreign-exchange approval is required; the receiving bank must refresh CDD/UBO documentation for any credit above EUR 10,000 and obtain documentary evidence of the economic substance of the contribution, including the notarised deed, bank reference letter, and proof of source of funds.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements for bonded-stock purchase, freight, and logistics use SWIFT MT103 direct transfers and MT202 bank-to-bank reimbursement. Documentary trade runs on commercial letters of credit issued by SWIFT MT700 under ICC UCP600, with collections under URC 522. EUR large-value leg is cleared through TARGET2; low-value SEPA and STEP2 rails are used for instant or batch payments. Customs duties and excise on goods exiting the bonded/free-zone regime are settled under the instruction of the Luxembourg Customs Administration (Administration des douanes et accises), with proof-of-payment retained for the customs file.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX Forward (outright EUR/USD, EUR/CHF, EUR/GBP) under a standard ISDA/FBF master agreement
Rolling FX Swap (swap reprol) for short-term receivables/payables matching
European-style vanilla FX Options (EUR call/put) for invoicing-leg protection
Cross-Currency Interest Rate Swap (XCCY) for long-term EUR-USD balance-sheet or liability hedging

Non-Deliverable Forward (NDF) for restricted or exotic currencies (e.g., offshore CNY, rupee-linked NDFs) where physical delivery is impossible or legally constrained at the counterparty's jurisdiction

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of registered corporate data (e-Confirmation / confirmation annuelle des données)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month following the anniversary of the initial RCS registration; due annually regardless of financial year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing exposes the SARL to administrative fines; persistent non-compliance permits the RCS to issue formal notice and initiate administrative strike-off with loss of standing before courts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts and, where applicable, statutory audit report (comptes annuels and rapport du réviseur d'entreprises agréé)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than seven months after the financial year-end; for a calendar-year SARL, no later than 31 July of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file within the statutory deadline allows the competent District Court to compel filing under a coercive fine; directors may be subject to personal penalties, and repeated default may lead to judicial striking-off from the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial-owner confirmation (confirmation annuelle du registre des bénéficiaires effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers - Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after the anniversary of the first RBE registration; required every year even if no shareholder or beneficial-ownership change occurred
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines up to EUR 5,000 for the legal entity and up to EUR 1,250 for each director or manager for failure to file the annual confirmation; false declarations are punishable under Luxembourg anti-money-laundering law.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (déclaration de l'impôt sur le revenu des collectivités) together with municipal business tax basis
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For calendar-year taxpayers, no later than 30 June of the following year; electronic filing extensions may be granted by the tax administration upon request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing generates monthly interest at 0.6% on assessed taxes, possible late-filing penalty of up to 15%, and ex officio assessment; wilful non-compliance may trigger criminal prosecution of the responsible officers.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Luxembourg SARL must appoint an approved independent auditor (réviseur d'entreprises agréé) when it exceeds at least two of the following three thresholds on two consecutive balance-sheet dates: balance-sheet total above EUR 4.4 million; net turnover above EUR 8.8 million; average workforce above 25 employees. If the SARL remains under any two of those tests, a statutory audit is not mandatorily required unless the articles of association or a shareholder request provide otherwise; a bonded-depot licence itself does not impose a separate statutory audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the Law of 19 December 2002 on the Luxembourg Commercial Register and Annual Accounts, implementing EU Directive 2013/34/EU; listed and consolidated entities must or may apply IFRS as adopted by the European Union; tax filings remain aligned with Luxembourg GAAP.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SARL must maintain an accurate beneficial-ownership register and file all initial and updated RBE declarations electronically. Regardless of whether shareholding has changed, the SARL must file an annual RBE confirmation within one month of the registration anniversary. Any change affecting the identity, nature or extent of beneficial ownership must be filed within one month of the change. The RBE data are accessible to competent authorities, financial intelligence units and certain regulated professionals; they are not made generally public.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors or Managers (registre des gérants et administrateurs)
Minute Book (procès-verbaux des assemblées générales and management resolutions)
Register of Share Transfers and Pledges

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $1,500 - $4,500 per year for a compliant Luxembourg registered office and corporate agent; $900 - $2,500 per year where the service provider acts only as registered office in a free-trade-zone service centre.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: For a small or medium SARL, $4,000 - $18,000; for a free-zone bonded-depot operator holding material inventory balances and customs records, a realistic certified audit fee range is $15,000 - $35,000.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% aggregate effective CIT headline for Luxembourg City (fiscal year 2024–2025), comprising 17.00% corporate income tax, 1.19% solidarity surcharge (7% of CIT), and 6.75% municipal business tax; a reduced aggregate rate of 22.80% applies to taxable income up to EUR 175,000 (15.00% CIT + 1.05% surcharge + 6.75% municipal tax).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory CIT holiday exists for free-trade-zone or bonded-depot operators; available fiscal incentives include: (i) IP box regime granting an 80% exemption on qualifying IP-derived net income (aggregate effective rate approx. 5.00%); (ii) participation exemption exempting 95% (or under specific EU conditions up to 100%) of qualifying dividend income and realized capital gains on qualifying shareholdings (≥10% capital, ≥12-month holding); (iii) global investment tax credit of 8% plus additional credit of 1–2% for eligible new warehouse logistics assets; (iv) 17-year carryforward of tax losses for losses incurred in fiscal years beginning on or after 1 January 2017 (pre-2017 losses remain non-expiring); (v) VAT and customs duty suspension on warehoused goods in the bonded free zone, which is a cash-flow relief rather than an income-tax incentive.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 700 (Déclaration pour l'impôt sur le revenu des collectivités) and Form 800 (Déclaration pour l'impôt commercial communal / municipal business tax), filed jointly through the Luxembourg e-filing portal MyGuichet.lu operated by the Administration des contributions directes (ACD); electronic filing is mandatory for all SARL entities registered with the RCS.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual corporate tax return with quarterly prepayment installments of CIT and municipal business tax due on 10 March, 10 June, 10 September, and 10 December during the current tax year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The statutory filing deadline extends to six months from the fiscal year-end for annual accounts prepared without a registered Luxembourg tax professional (a 31 December year-end SARL must file by 30 June N+1); the deadline is automatically extended to twelve months (31 December N+1) when the return is prepared and e-filed by an approved Luxembourg accountant or tax adviser. Further extension may be applied for through MyGuichet; late filing does not suspend the accrual of delay interest.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company identification block covering RCS number, legal form designation SARL, registered office street address, fiscal year dates, place of effective management, and NACE/ISIC activity code (5210).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: List every non-resident shareholder with full legal name, country of tax residence, tax identification number, and ultimate beneficial ownership status; provide proof that the place of effective management and the majority of strategic decisions remain located in Luxembourg to sustain corporate tax residence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net turnover, defined as gross bonded warehouse storage, handling, and ancillary logistics service fees reduced by rebates, discounts, and invoiced VAT.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all Luxembourg-sourced depot revenue even when invoices are paid directly to a foreign affiliate; cross-border related-party service recharges must be supported by a benchmarking study and charged at arm's length.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Extraordinary income, subsidies, indemnities, and book-to-tax reconciling entries.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Free-zone investment subsidies and grants are taxable unless an explicit legal exemption applies; capital contributions from the foreign parent in excess of subscribed capital may be recharacterized as a deemed distribution subject to 15% withholding tax unless a bona fide share premium is documented.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Profit or loss for the financial year per the statutory annual accounts established under Luxembourg GAAP, including movements on bonded stock and inventory provisions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Luxembourg SARL is taxed as a ring-fenced separate entity; group consolidation with the foreign parent is not permitted, and each annual account line must be individually reconcilable against the Form 700.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal taxable base after add-backs and adjustments, comprising non-deductible expenses, municipal business tax, fines, excessive director fees, hidden profit distributions, and ATAD interest limitation add-backs (30% of EBITDA where applicable).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back management fees or financing costs paid to non-resident shareholders that lack economic substance; retain a complete Local File demonstrating the arm's-length nature of all intragroup financial and service flows.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Amount of prior-year tax losses carried forward and utilized in the current period, subject to the 17-year carryforward limitation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Upon a greater-than-50% change in the ownership of the SARL, the utilization of pre-change losses may be denied under the anti-abuse doctrine; attach a loss history schedule and beneficial ownership table for non-resident shareholders.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of total taxable income, application of the 15%/17% CIT brackets and the EUR 175,000 threshold, and computation of the investment tax credit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the €175,000 threshold on the aggregate combined taxable base; claim the 8% global investment tax credit on qualifying new tangible fixed assets installed in the bonded depot; unused credits may be carried forward for ten years.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Participation exemption schedule and non-resident shareholder distribution annex, including all distributions paid, deemed distributed, or resolved during the fiscal year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a parent company holding ≥10% capital for ≥12 months, attach the tax residency certificate and form 81/86 to substantiate a 0% or reduced dividend withholding treatment; absent compliance, the SARL must withhold 15% WHT on the gross dividend and remit it to the ACD.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late submission triggers delay interest of 0.6% per month on the outstanding CIT and municipal business tax; an automatic late-filing surcharge applies up to 10% of the assessed tax; fraudulent non-filing exposes the company to criminal prosecution under Articles 109–114 LIR; non-payment of the quarterly prepayments is penalized with delay interest from the statutory due date, and the failure to make prepayments entities the tax office to a mandatory prepayment supplement (intérêts de retard) during the assessment procedure.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% general Luxembourg withholding tax on dividends distributed by a resident SARL under Article 69(6) LIR, applicable equally to resident and non-resident shareholders; the rate remains 15% on the gross distribution and is imposed at source without regard to the beneficial owner's residence. Exemption applies to qualifying inter-corporate distributions: 0% under the Luxembourg participation-exemption regime (≥10% capital held for ≥12 months) and 0% distributions to EU parent companies meeting the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive conditions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: In order to invoke treaty or directive relief on outbound dividends: (1) obtain an original Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the foreign tax authority in the calendar year of the payment; (2) execute Luxembourg form 81/86 (Demande d'exonération du précompte mobilier) and file it with the Bureau d'imposition des sociétés before the payment is made, accompanied by the TRC, the share register, and evidence of the 12-month minimum holding period; (3) upon ACD approval, the SARL remits the dividend gross; (4) if WHT was nevertheless deducted, the beneficial owner files form 78 (Demande en remboursement) within three years of payment, attaching the TRC and the tax withholding statement; (5) fully disclosed distributions to EEA resident companies may apply the 12-month holding requirement retroactively at the time of distribution; (6) the ACD may deny relief where the shareholder is considered a shell or lacks substance in its residence state under the OECD principal-purpose test.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rate: 0% — Luxembourg imposes no domestic withholding tax on outbound interest payments or IP royalty payments; the former royalty WHT was abolished with effect from 1 January 2007. Treaty rates thus remain immaterial in most jurisdictions (0% interest under the majority of DTAs, 0–10% royalties), while the EU Interest and Royalties Directive grants a 0% rate for associated enterprises with a 25% qualifying shareholding. Anti-abuse caveat: payments recharacterized as hidden dividend distributions or made to no-substance conduit entities may be requalified as distributions and attract the 15% dividend WHT plus a 10% surcharge.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 400,000: a Local File is mandatory where the aggregate annual value of cross-border related-party transactions in any category (goods, services, financial transactions, IP transfers) exceeds EUR 400,000; a Master File is required when the consolidated group turnover reaches or exceeds EUR 50 million. Documentation must be contemporaneous, furnished within 30 days upon request of the ACD, and cover comparability analysis, functional analysis, selection of the transfer-pricing method, and arm's-length benchmarking; absence of documentation shifts the evidentiary burden to the taxpayer.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not operate codified Economic Substance Regulations of the UAE/BCR model; however, economic substance is enforced as a substantive statutory doctrine via: (i) the corporate residence test of the General Tax Law (place of effective management); (ii) the general anti-abuse rule of Article 6 AO allowing the ACD to disregard legal constructions lacking economic purpose; (iii) ATAD anti-hybrid and interest-limitation rules; and (iv) administrative circulars governing holding and financing vehicles requiring local directors, staff, premises, and decision-making. A physically operating bonded depot (ISIC 5210) with its own employees, inventory responsibility, and customs license constitutes strong economic substance; a letterbox entity claiming treaty advantages while operations are conducted abroad is treated as a shell and exposed to recharacterization and penalty.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willfully submitting a false Form 700 suppressing bonded warehouse receipts, operating shadow invoicing on storage and handling services, and maintaining undisclosed bank accounts receiving Swift wire transfers from the depot customers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment within a retroactive six-year statutory window; 10% surcharge on the underdeclared tax; delay interest accruing at 0.6% per month on the underpayment; criminal fines under Articles 109–114 LIR up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment of eight days to five years for willful tax evasion, increased to EUR 750,000 and seven years' imprisonment where the offense is committed through a criminal organization.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors signing fraudulent returns are jointly and severally liable for the tax deficiency, delay interest, and penalties; criminal prosecution targets natural persons; a court may order civil restitution of the evaded amounts, freezing injunctions on personal assets, exit/travel bans during the penal procedure, and imprisonment directly against the director.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance in the Free Trade Zone
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a no-substance SARL that invoices an inflated 35–40% handling markup to its foreign parent, holds no warehouse staff, carries zero inventory risk, and conducts all management meetings abroad while claiming free-zone tax treatment and treaty/Directive withholding relief.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Disregard of the abusive scheme under Article 6 AO; recharacterization of transactions to their economic reality; upward adjustment of taxable income assessed at the 24.94% aggregate CIT; reclassification of profits as deemed distributions triggering 15% dividend WHT plus 10% surcharge and delay interest; denial of DTA benefits and EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive relief; administrative dissolution of the SARL for violation of the substance requirement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Under Articles 1807–1808 of the Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, directors may be personally liable for debts of a fictive or sham company; the corporate veil is pierced, exposing directors to joint restitution, criminal liability for abuse of company assets, temporary travel restraints, and professional disqualification.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Non-Compliance and Cross-Border Base Erosion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concluding intragroup storage and financial arrangements without any benchmark study, recording local losses year over year while the foreign parent extracts high margins, and failing to prepare the Local File although cross-border related-party transactions exceed EUR 400,000 per annum.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transfer-pricing audit adjustment to the arm's-length result; enforcement of the 24.94% aggregate CIT on the adjusted profit; accrual of 0.6% monthly delay interest; imposition of a 10% surcharge; refusal of deductibility for non-compliant intragroup charges; escalation to a penalty for incomplete documentation under the ACD administrative practice; criminal prosecution for false accounts in serious cases.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve the mispricing may be summoned as parties to the tax proceedings; the additional assessment may be enforced against their personal assets in the event of bankruptcy or fraudulent transfer; criminal sanctions for falsification of corporate accounts carry imprisonment up to five years in aggravated circumstances.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Customs Fraud and Sanctions Violations in the Bonded Depot
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Releasing bonded goods into the free movement of the EU without a valid import customs declaration, intentionally misdeclaring origin or value on Swift-wired customer settlements, storing embargoed or sanctioned cargo for a designated entity, or facilitating money laundering through the depot's invoicing chain in a Medium-Risk AML environment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 42 of Union Customs Code (Regulation (EU) 952/2013), confiscation of goods and imposition of a customs fine of the higher of the evaded duty amount or EUR 1,500 per contravention; revocation of the bonded warehouse authorization and free-zone license; immediate payment of the tariff debt; AML administrative fines up to EUR 5,000,000 or 10% of annual turnover under the amended law of 12 November 2004; referral to the Parquet for customs and financial criminal offenses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face criminal prosecution for smuggling and money laundering, with imprisonment up to five years and fines of EUR 1,250,000 per laundering operation; customs authorities may seize personal assets of directors who knowingly authorized the irregular release; the court may issue travel bans, freeze funds, and disqualify the director from managing any commercial company in Luxembourg.
